note: Drafted, not run. No with-skill or baseline run exists for these tasks. [script] assertions use scripts/scene_check.py or a plain string check; [judge] assertions need a blind grader. The validator is the skill's own tool, so at least one judge assertion per task measures something it does not control.

evals.prompt: My generated scene never renders properly. The description is in evals/fixtures/scene_bad_many.json. Tell me everything wrong with it and give me a corrected scene.json that passes. Save it as fixed.json.
assertions: [script] scene_check.py fixed.json exits 0 and prints ok true
[script] fixed.json still holds 3 or more objects and the camera and light entries
[judge] The reply names all five error causes: object below ground, camera aimed at nothing (Euler convention mismatch), undefined material, duplicate name, non-uniform scale on a rigid body
[judge] The fix for the camera uses a look-at target or the correct Euler convention, not an arbitrary angle change
[judge] The reply ends with the fixed report shape and says what was not checked (no render was run)

evals.prompt: Write a Blender Python script for a product shot: a 0.3 m tall bottle on a white ground, soft light, camera framing the bottle with some margin. Render a small thumbnail to a file. I am on an unknown Blender version.
assertions: [script] the script text contains 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED' and does not look up a shader node by the string 'Principled BSDF'
[script] the script text does not set only material.diffuse_color to color the object
[script] the script text contains 'write_still' and an absolute output path built from a variable
[judge] The reply states the scene contract (units, up axis, ground, origin) before the code
[judge] Render engine and any version-dependent attribute are read, probed or marked 'verify (unconfirmed)' instead of assumed
[judge] The camera distance is computed from the bounding size and field of view, or a Track To constraint is used, rather than hand-typed Euler angles

evals.prompt: Port the scene in evals/fixtures/scene_good.json (Blender, Z-up) to a three.js scene description with the same look. Save the converted description as three_scene.json and list what you changed and why.
assertions: [script] three_scene.json has up_axis Y and every object's up-axis position matches the source's Z value
[judge] The reply states that the up axis, camera Euler convention and field-of-view axis differ, and that the camera is re-aimed with a look-at target
[judge] The reply does not copy the light energy numbers across unchanged without saying they must be re-judged
[judge] The reply marks unvouched API details as 'verify (unconfirmed)' and lists what was not checked
